thread.title: How to use R to scrape financials from Yahoo Finance

author: FrankUnderwood268
title: How to use R to scrape financials from Yahoo Finance
text:
With dplyr , rvest , tibble and purrr we can do: library(dplyr) library(purrr) library(rvest) library(tibble) "https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AAPL/financials?p=AAPL" %>% read_html() %>% html_table() %>% map_df(bind_cols) %>% as_tibble() # A tibble: 28 x 5 X1 X2 X3 X4 X5 <chr><chr><chr><chr><chr> 1 Revenue 9/30/2017 9/24/2016 9/26/2015 9/27/20… 2 Total Revenue 229,234,000 215,639,000 233,715,000 182,795… 3 Cost of Revenue 141,048,000 131,376,000 140,089,000 112,258… 4 Gross Profit 88,186,000 84,263,000 93,626,000 70,537,… 5 Operating Expenses Operating Expenses Operating Expenses Operating Expenses Operati… 6 Research Development 11,581,000 10,045,000 8,067,000 6,041,0… 7 Selling General and Administrative 15,261,000 14,194,000 14,329,000 11,993,… 8 Non Recurring - - - - 9 Others - - - - 10 Total Operating Expenses 167,890,000 155,615,000 162,485,000 130,292… # ... with 18 more rows 
Note that if you want to take the first row and treat it as a column name, add header = TRUE to the html_table call: html_table(header = TRUE) . This will give you the dates as column names in the finances data frame for example. 
If you want to combine the three tables into a data frame with nested data we could use enframe from the tibble package: balance <- "https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AAPL/balance-sheet?p=AAPL" %>% read_html() %>% html_table() %>% map_df(bind_cols) %>% as_tibble() finances <- "https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AAPL/financials?p=AAPL" %>% read_html() %>% html_table() %>% map_df(bind_cols) %>% as_tibble() cash_flow <- "https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AAPL/cash-flow?p=AAPL" %>% read_html() %>% html_table() %>% map_df(bind_cols) %>% as_tibble() list(balance, finances, cash_flow) %>% enframe() %>% mutate(name = c("balance", "finances", "cash_flow")) # A tibble: 3 x 2 name value <chr><list> 1 balance <tibble [38 × 5]> 2 finances <tibble [28 × 5]> 3 cash_flow <tibble [23 × 5]> 
If you choose to do this, you will need the tidyr package to unnest the data.
